findings.detail: A failed upstream lookup with no returned data becomes a successful empty result through `|| true`. The empty-latest branch records no unavailable state. When no other surface contributes drift, the script exits successfully with empty stdout, and its companion workflow closes an existing drift issue as cleared despite the incomplete audit. Making stderr visible does not prevent that action. This defect predates the change, was independently confirmed at the immutable base, and retains its previously recorded Important severity.
findings.evidence: Lines 206–211 convert a failed Node lookup into empty latest followed by a successful return. Lines 742–744 emit nothing when drift_rows is empty. The companion version-audit-workflow-template.yml maps empty stdout to has_drift=false and closes an open audit issue. Other runtime and registry helpers use the same failure-to-empty pattern.
findings.title: Absent or partial data: upstream failures still become a no-drift success

findings.detail: A Copilot concern in comment position 21 through 100 of an unresolved Copilot-opened thread is omitted by both retrieval paths. fetch returns only the first 20 comments, while audit indexes the first 100 and treats their membership in that thread as coverage by fetch. No nested pagination metadata identifies the longer thread for the documented manual fallback. This defect predates the change, was independently confirmed at the immutable base, and retains its previously recorded Important severity.
findings.evidence: do_fetch requests comments(first: 20) at line 241; fetch_thread_index requests comments(first: 100) at line 646. do_parse_audit indexes those comments at lines 555–564, then emits no uncovered entry for an indexed comment in a Copilot-opened thread at lines 575–584. Thus a concern appearing only in comment 21 is neither fetched nor reported as uncovered.
findings.title: Parallel paths: the audit hides replies beyond the fetcher's comment cap

Groups: code and docs, with agent-facing tailoring guidance in the version-audit template. Result: 2 Important findings, both previously recorded and pre-existing at the immutable base. Their severity is preserved. No additional Important findings were identified. This completed batch is not clean at Important.

Siblings examined for the unavailable-version finding: all twelve template audit functions, GitHub release/tag fallbacks, npm/crates.io/PyPI helpers, scan producers, print_report, bin/version-audit, the companion workflow template, and the tailoring and issue-management documentation.

Siblings examined for the comment-cap finding: do_fetch, fetch_thread_index, do_parse_audit, do_fetch_reviews, the resolver's longer-thread fallback and completion criteria, monitor feedback projections, and related Scrut cases and fixtures. Comments 21–100 fall between the two coverage limits; comments beyond 100 instead appear absent from the index.

Other paths examined included Dependabot pagination and partial-file reporting, unavailable comparisons and alerts, merge-flow capture and structured errors, watch counters and lifecycle handling, watch-policy gates, sync ancestry checks, test registration, and offline fixture request validation.
